facts.raw_span: 48-year-old white man
lifelong non-smoker
remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid 17 years earlier
three-month history of mild hemoptysis
cough without dyspnea
non-tender, 2 × 2 cm subcutaneous mass on his left forearm
oxygen saturation of 94% on room air
complete blood count, liver and renal function tests, and coagulation profile, were all within normal limits
polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region adjacent to the anterior wall
mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall just above the main carina, causing an 80% obstruction of the right main bronchus and 70% obstruction of the left main bronchus
tumor consisted of large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix
carcinoid tumor was initially suspected

concepts.why: The patient has a history of a remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid and presents with a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which is consistent with a tracheal carcinoid tumor.
The patient has a subcutaneous mass on his left forearm, which could be a metastasis from the tracheal carcinoid tumor.
The patient has a three-month history of mild hemoptysis and cough without dyspnea, which is consistent with a chronic cough.

The patient has a mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall, causing an 80% obstruction of the right main bronchus and 70% obstruction of the left main bronchus, which is consistent with tracheal obstruction.
The patient has a three-month history of mild hemoptysis, which is consistent with hemoptysis.
The patient has a non-tender, 2 × 2 cm subcutaneous mass on his left forearm, which could be a subcutaneous lipoma.
The patient has a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which is consistent with a tracheal tumor.

The patient has a mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall, causing an 80% obstruction of the right main bronchus and 70% obstruction of the left main bronchus, which is consistent with bronchial obstruction.

rationales.F03: Previous history of tracheal carcinoid tumor increases the likelihood of another tracheal carcinoid tumor.
rationales.F04: Hemoptysis is a common symptom of tracheal carcinoid tumors and tracheal obstructions.
rationales.F06: Subcutaneous mass could be a metastasis or a separate entity like a lipoma.
rationales.F09: Polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region is suggestive of a tracheal tumor.
rationales.F10: Mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall causing obstruction is highly suggestive of a tracheal tumor.
rationales.F11: Histological description of large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix is characteristic of carcinoid tumors.
rationales.F12: Initial suspicion of carcinoid tumor based on histological findings increases the likelihood of a tracheal carcinoid tumor.
